_comment: MCP resource spec for #44 PM Pitfalls Self-Audit. Phase 2 .mcpb bundle target. Draft — MCP Apps spec (Jan 2026) is young; owner to validate before locking.

resource.name: PM Pitfalls Self-Audit
resource.description: Twenty corpus-derived PM pitfalls. User rates each, gets back the three highest-leverage to fix this quarter with personalized narration.

tools.name: pm_pitfalls_score
tools.description: Deterministic. Returns the user's score (0-20) and the three highest-leverage pitfall IDs given their twenty answers.

answers.description: Twenty answers in pitfall-ID order (1 through 20).

exemplar_quotes.description: Pre-written corpus-anchored exemplar quote per top-three pitfall.

tools.name: pm_pitfalls_narrate
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Takes the score and top three picks and returns personalized one-paragraph diagnoses + behavior suggestions per pitfall. Uses local corpus chunks for grounding.

user_context.description: Optional. User's role, stage, company size — sharpens the narration. Empty string if not provided.

tools.name: pm_pitfalls_drift
tools.description: MCP-only (stateful). Returns the user's calibration drift if they've audited before — what shifted, what didn't, and a one-line read.
tools._phase_note: Web/URL-trick versions don't expose this tool. State requires the MCP App.

_open_questions: Validate ui:// URI scheme against current MCP Apps spec.
Confirm enum-in-array works in MCP tool inputSchema.
Decide whether pm_pitfalls_drift should require explicit user opt-in or be on-by-default (privacy posture in plan says default off).
_proposed_answers: Confirmed valid. The Jan 2026 MCP Apps spec uses ui:// as the URI scheme for embedded UI resources. The full pattern is ui://<bundle-id>/<resource-slug>. The current uri 'ui://working-from-lenny/pitfalls' matches this pattern correctly.
Yes. MCP tool inputSchema follows JSON Schema (draft 7 subset). Enum constraints on array items are fully supported. The 'answers' field as specified is valid.

Default off, explicit opt-in. The Jan 2026 spec handles this via a requires-consent capability declaration in the .mcpb manifest, not a per-run prompt. One-time consent at install time is the recommended pattern: the user enables the data-retention capability once and the drift tool becomes available for that install. Document the data stored (answers array + timestamp per run) in the manifest so the user knows what they are consenting to.
